name: Molded Products Inc
old_description: Molded Products was founded in 1986, initially focused on providing rubber molded goods for the automotive aftermarket.
about:
Molded Products Inc was founded in 1986 in Broken Arrow, Oklahoma, initially supplying rubber molded goods to the automotive aftermarket. The company began as a focused rubber molding operation and has since expanded its capabilities.

Today the company operates as a diversified custom rubber molder specializing in compression molding, transfer molding, and rubber-to-metal bonding. Its 22 hydraulic presses range up to 600 tons, supported by in-house tool and die machining, preforming equipment (including 60-inch and 50-inch mills, Barwell extruders), finishing lines with cryogenic deflashing, a paint center, and general machining. The facility runs 24 hours a day, five days a week, enabling quick turnaround on urgent jobs.

Molded Products serves a range of industrial markets including oil and gas, construction, fuel-cell seals, electrical, automotive and aftermarket, aerospace, and air filtration. Customers rely on the shop for turn-key solutions that span concept, tooling design, prototype development, and full production runs.

The company emphasizes its ISO 9001:2015 certified quality system, in-house tooling control, and a reputation for delivering quality, timely, and cost-competitive rubber components. Its founding aim was to provide reliable molded rubber parts, and it has maintained that focus while broadening its industrial reach.

name: Molding Products
old_description: Founded in 1978, Molding Products LLC, an operating business of IP Corporation, supplies sheet molding composites (SMC) to the growing compression molding industry. Today, the company remains focused on providing industry-leading, custom-formulated molding compounds for a wide variety of industries and applications.
about:
Molding Products LLC was founded in 1978 in South Bend, Indiana, as an operating business of IP Corporation. The company began by supplying sheet molding composites (SMC) to the growing compression molding industry and remains focused on custom-formulated molding compounds for diverse applications.

The company produces custom and standard sheet molding compounds (SMC) and other engineered thermoset materials. Its services include material formulation, technical support, prototype tooling via strategic alliances, mold design and construction, onsite mold evaluation, and compression press prototyping. Molding Products operates a manufacturing facility in South Bend with a technical team that includes quality, engineering, and sales staff. The facility uses a programmable logic control system to monitor processes and conducts quality testing on every sheet of compound.

Molding Products serves industries such as aerospace, automotive, communications, construction, electrical, heavy-duty truck, HVAC, industrial furniture, marine, pallets, sanitary, sporting goods, swimming pools, transportation, infrastructure, building and construction, and consumer markets. A 2022 agreement with NanoXplore added graphene-enhanced SMC for battery enclosures and lightweight composite exteriors.

The company differentiates itself by not being a custom molder, avoiding competition with its customers, and maintaining project confidentiality. A central Indiana location is noted to minimize freight costs.

about:
Moldrite Products Inc operates from Colorado Springs, Colorado. The company was founded on the principle of valuing American-made products and labor, a philosophy that remains central to its identity. It is a family-owned business that has been operating for over 25 years, though a specific founding year is not publicly disclosed.

The company specializes in plastic injection molding, offering a full range of services from mold conception and construction to production and storage. Materials processed include ABS, styrene, engineering-grade resins such as Cycoloy, Lexan, and Noryl, as well as custom-colored, UV-inhibited, and UL-approved formulations. Additional capabilities include mold storage, machine shop maintenance, and consulting.

Moldrite serves a diverse customer base across industries requiring custom plastic components, though specific sectors are not detailed in its public materials. The company emphasizes its ability to handle projects of any size, from initial design through final delivery.

Differentiators highlighted by the company include a 100% satisfaction guarantee, round-the-clock customer service, and a commitment to competitive pricing versus overseas alternatives. All products are manufactured in the United States, and the production facility is OSHA compliant.

name: Montana Specialty Mills
old_description: At Montana Specialty Mills, we process and market high quality oilseeds and specialty products. We adhere to rigorous standards in crop sourcing, processing operations, and customer service. Working directly with local growers ensures consistent access to the best production inputs. Our oilseed products are used as ingredients in a variety of foods that ultimately make their way to families’ kitchens across North America and beyond.
about:
Montana Specialty Mills operates oilseed processing facilities in Great Falls and Conrad, Montana. The company was established in 1997 as a joint venture between Columbia Grain International, a global grain and pulse supplier based in Portland, Oregon, and Nisshin OilliO America, part of a Japanese edible-oil manufacturing group. The partnership combined Columbia Grain’s sourcing network with Nisshin OilliO’s processing expertise to serve North American food ingredient markets.

The mills specialize in cleaning, crushing, and refining oilseeds into organic and non-GMO oils, meals, and hulls for food manufacturers. Their facilities are described as state-of-the-art, though specific capacity figures are not disclosed. The company manages the full chain from crop sourcing through processing operations, emphasizing rigorous quality standards at each step.

End-use customers include bakeries, food-service distributors, repackers, food manufacturers, and industrial manufacturers across North America. On the supply side, Montana Specialty Mills contracts directly with growers in the United States and Canada, offering multi-year growing programs designed to provide stable returns and reliable delivery.

The venture was formed to bridge regional growers with large-scale food ingredient buyers, promising consistent product quality, flexibility in order fulfillment, and dependable service. The company highlights its long-term grower partnerships and direct-from-farm traceability as key differentiators.

name: Montebello Plastics
old_description: Montebello Plastics specializes in high-quality polyethylene film solutions designed for a variety of
about:
Montebello Plastics operates from Montebello, California. The company was founded in 2019 and is a small business; co‑founder Nado Husa is named on the leadership team. While the current entity dates to 2019, the team brings over four decades of experience in plastic film manufacturing.

The company manufactures polyethylene film products — custom poly bags, tubing, and sheeting — using high‑density (HDPE), low‑density (LDPE), and linear low‑density (LLDPE) resins. All items are made to order; no stock is kept. Production capabilities include custom sizing, thickness, color, and specialty additives such as PCR/reprocessed material, nano‑enhanced technology, and a bioremediation additive that breaks down to zero microplastics. The minimum order is typically one pallet (about 1,000 lbs).

Montebello Plastics serves industrial packaging, construction, agriculture, and the laundry/cleaners supply sector. Named customers include Laundry & Cleaners Supply, Inc., Continental Western Corporation, and AMZ Packaging, Inc. The company ships nationwide and offers local truck delivery in the Inland Empire, Orange County, Los Angeles, and the San Fernando Valley.

The company emphasizes that every product is 100% recyclable and meets California SB54 requirements. It highlights free shipping on U.S. orders over $50, a dedicated team that answers calls and emails same‑day, and a commitment to recycling all production scrap. FDA‑approved films are available for applicable applications.

name: Monterey Mills
old_description: Sliver knitting, or high-pile knitting, is a process that locks individual fibers into a lightweight knit backing. The length of acrylic fibers used adds dimension and warmth to the fabric, when needed, without adding additional weight. Other advantages of using acrylic fibers include the incorporation of colorfast dyes and, a finished fabric that is odor and mildew resistant. The end result is a light, soft, comfortable fabric that is warmer than fleece and is machine washable and dryable.
about:
Monterey Mills operates from Janesville, Wisconsin. The company traces its current ownership to February 1995, when Dan Sinykin purchased the former Roller Fabrics after a seven-month unpaid trial period. Sinykin, a Drake University graduate, had previously built a 14-store retail tailor chain and spent six years in sales and marketing at Procter & Gamble. He consolidated multiple manufacturing facilities and expanded the business into automotive, equestrian, apparel, hospital, and pet-product markets.

The mill specializes in sliver knitting (also called high-pile knitting), a labor-intensive process that locks individual acrylic fibers into a lightweight knit backing to create fabrics that are warmer than fleece yet machine washable. An in-house research and development team controls fiber and yarn selection, pile height, density, tensile strength, width, color, and stitch count, enabling custom performance fabrics for diverse applications. The company produces rolled fabrics, paint-roller fabrics, and finished goods for medical, pet, blanket, and bedding lines, all marketed as Made in USA.

Customers span medical and pet-product manufacturers, blanket and bedding brands, automotive and equestrian suppliers, apparel makers, and hospital procurement. The technical team works directly with clients to develop fabrics that meet specific performance requirements, from odor and mildew resistance to colorfastness.

Monterey Mills positions itself as one of the few remaining practitioners of sliver knitting, a craft many competitors abandoned due to its complexity. The company emphasizes sustainability, sourcing recycled raw materials, repurposing all production waste, and treating and reusing wastewater. Continuous improvement in processes and employee skills is cited as the foundation for its quality reputation.

name: Montrose Molders
old_description: Montrose has been in business since 1966, is ISO9001 certified, and has a large and broad injection molding fleet.
about:
Montrose Molders operates from Piscataway, New Jersey, where it was founded in 1966 by William Bruce Wilson. The company began as a 22-person tool shop producing tight-tolerance molds for the plastics industry and added its first injection molding press in 1972. Today it remains a family-owned business led by the Wilson family, now in its fourth generation of plastics manufacturing.

The firm runs a vertically integrated operation that covers part design, tooling, molding, extrusion, assembly, and packaging. Its molding department comprises 51 presses ranging from 40 to 1,000 tons of clamp force, supported by two extrusion lines with co-extrusion capability. An on-site tool room builds aluminum and steel production molds, while a 25,000-square-foot assembly area can run five lines simultaneously. Mold-flow simulation uses SolidWorks Plastics software, and industrial design services help translate concepts into 3D models.

Montrose serves customers in retail, battery, automotive, lighting, safety, aerospace, electronics, medical devices, and consumer goods. The company positions itself as a contract plastics manufacturer for original equipment manufacturers and brand owners seeking a single-source partner from prototype through full-scale production.

Management emphasizes a one-stop-shop model intended to shorten lead times, reduce costs, and deliver consistent quality. Each program is assigned a dedicated project manager, and engineering resources span industrial design to tooling validation. The family legacy is cited as a driver of long-term customer relationships and continuous investment in equipment and process control.

name: More Than A Bakery
old_description: Delivering high-quality food manufacturing solutions and fostering our community since 1855.
about:
More Than A Bakery operates from Versailles, Kentucky, as part of a family-owned contract manufacturing group with roots tracing back to 1855 in Richmond, Indiana. The business was founded in 1855 and has remained family-operated across generations, delivering food manufacturing solutions while fostering community ties.

The group runs two bakery facilities producing cookies, crackers, and a broad line of crumb and coating products for food service and industrial clients. Core capabilities include custom crumb and coating formulation, R&D support, and product scale-up services. Finished goods are packaged in bag-in-a-box, kraft bags, or super sacks to accommodate a range of order sizes.

Primary customers are food service suppliers and other food manufacturers that need reliable contract production of bakery items and ingredient blends. The company’s crumb and coating products are used in applications such as breading, toppings, and inclusions for prepared foods.

Leadership frames the operation as “more than just facilities,” emphasizing a mission to give back to families, friends, and neighbors. Stated values—family, passion, gratitude, purposeful growth, and integrity—guide a culture that prioritizes employee well-being and work-life balance alongside production goals.

name: Moriden America, Inc.
old_description: Moriden America, Inc. was founded in the United States in 1988 and began operations in Detroit Michigan in 1989. Our company opened operations in Indianapolis a year later, and in 1993 moved all operations to Indianapolis, Indiana.
about:
Moriden America, Inc. is headquartered in Carmel, Indiana. The company was founded in 1988 as a U.S. subsidiary of Moriden Company LTD, a Japanese firm with over 80 years of experience in automotive, transportation, and furniture products. Operations began in Detroit, Michigan, in 1989, expanded to Indianapolis a year later, and consolidated in Indianapolis in 1993 before moving to the current Carmel location.

The company manufactures automotive interior fabric and trim components across three main product lines: seating materials, interior trim, and cargo systems. Its processes include compression molding of coated carpets with soft trim and hardware, high-strength reaction injection molding (HS-RIM) for luggage floor boards on an integrated production line, and simulation-driven upholstery design. The facility houses design, development, production, quality control, and logistics operations.

Moriden America supplies the North American automotive industry with decorative and functional trim parts such as trunk trim, shift boots, seat upholstery, mat floors, rear seat backs, and tonneau covers. Its customers are vehicle manufacturers and tier suppliers seeking lightweight, high-strength composites and flexible production that can respond quickly to changing model requirements.

The company states that its differentiation lies in a commitment to continuous improvement across safety, quality, cost, delivery, and management. It emphasizes optimizing product design through deep knowledge of material and process selection, and providing fast, consistent service from development proposal through to sales.

name: Moulstown Woodworks
old_description: Moulstown Woodworks is nestled in the Pigeon Hills of York County just east of Abbottstown, PA and from our log yard we take the portable sawmill service anywhere. Our motto is “can mill, will travel” which runs on the back of a 2021 Woodmizer LT40, fully hydraulic, commercial portable sawmill with a wide saw head that clears a 34” cut and up to 20’ log lengths.
about:
Moulstown Woodworks operates from a log yard in the Pigeon Hills of York County, just east of Abbottstown, Pennsylvania. The business is run by Wade, who offers a mobile sawmilling service under the motto “can mill, will travel.” No founding year or ownership structure is disclosed on the company’s website.

The core service is on-site portable sawmilling using a 2021 Woodmizer LT40, a fully hydraulic commercial mill with a 34-inch cutting width and capacity for logs up to 20 feet long. The mill can lift and turn logs up to 4,000 pounds; heavier logs require crane assistance. Typical output runs 250–300 board feet per hour, with milling priced at $75 per hour plus a transportation and setup fee starting at $85 for sites within 10 miles of the yard. The company also provides yield estimates and pre‑job site visits.

Customers include landowners, arborists, excavators, forestry consultants, lumber buyers, kiln operators, furniture makers, carpenters, and luthiers across south‑central Pennsylvania (Adams, Cumberland, Perry, Lancaster, Chester, and York counties) and northern Maryland (Frederick, Carroll, Baltimore, and Hartford counties). Repeat clients are noted in towns such as Gettysburg, Hanover, New Oxford, and Westminster.

The business emphasizes customer preparation—clean, metal‑free logs staged for the mill, adequate labor to clear slabs, and equipment to move heavy logs—as the key to efficient yield. The mobile model eliminates the need for customers to transport logs to a fixed mill.
